items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the public service law, in relation to certain requirements
regarding billing for electric services
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1979

SPONSOR: JACKSON
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public service law, in relation to certain require-
ments regarding billing for electric services

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to provide pricing transparency of electric
bills for residents and businesses, and to provide customers with better
predictability of future electric bills.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 adds a new subdivision 29 to Section 66 of the Public Service
Law to provide that the manner and method in which customers are billed
for their electrical use.

Section 2 amends subdivision 14 of Section 66 of the Public Service Law
to provide that classifications of service must be indicated on custom-
ers' bills for electric service and must include the website address to
the specific public service commission leaf.

Section 3 amends subdivision 1 of Section 44 of the Public Service Law
to provide that detailed line item transparency and peak pricing of that
item over the preceding 52-week period.

Section 4 adds a new subdivision 6 to Section 44 of the Public Service
Law to provide that customers that currently receive electronic data
interchange by protocols approved by the commission shall be exempt from
receiving printed bill statements if such customer's aggregate annual
demand per year exceeds three megawatts. Additionally, printed billing
statements are not required to be sent if both the customer and the
vendor are state public benefit corporations.

Section 4 also adds a new subdivision 7 to Section 44 of the Public
Service Law to provide a disclosure notice regarding demand delivery
charges.

Section 5 adds a new Section 52-A to the Public Service Law that
provides the manner and method in which residential rental building
submetering may be implemented.

Section 6 amends subdivision 3 of Section 38 of the Public Service Law
to provide that every utility corporation or municipality must notify
residential customers within 90 days of the level billing period if the
utility corporation projects a shortfall at the end of the level billing
period.

Section 7 is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This legislation aims to provide transparency in the billing of residen-
tial and commercial electric customers. This level of transparency will
allow both residential and small businesses to understand how they get
billed for energy consumption and what different actions customers can
take to lower their bills and be able to project costs over time.
Currently, very few users that have a demand delivery component in their
bill fully understand all the different line items of their bill and how
their total bill amount can change drastically based on the way the user
modifies their energy use. This legislation would make the energy bills
easier to read and to help residents and businesses save money while
simultaneously reducing the amount of standby power that needs to be
generated across the state, which indirectly would require less CO' to
be sent into the atmosphere.  This legislation also protects tenants
that are subject to submetering by a third party, in many cases an enti-
ty connected to their landlord, from being ineligible for public assist-
ance and other programs because the billing entity is not the operator
of the local power transmission network.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019-2020: S.7708 - Passed the Senate

 
STATE AND LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the one hundred eightieth day after it
shall have become a law. Effective immediately, the addition, amendment
and/or repeal of any rule or regulation necessary for the implementation
of this act on its effective date are authorized to be made and
completed on or before such date.

BILL NUMBER: S1979a

SPONSOR: JACKSON
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public service law, in relation to certain require-

TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public service law, in relation to certain require-
ments regarding billing for electric services

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to provide pricing transparency of electric
bills for residents and businesses, and to provide customers with better
predictability of future electric bills.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends subdivision 14 of Section 66 of the Public Service Law
to provide that classifications of service must be indicated on custom-
ers' bills for electric service and must include the website address to
the specific public service commission leaf.

Section 2 amends subdivision 1 of Section 44 of the Public Service Law
to require that utility bills for residential and demand-metered custom-
ers include certain information to allow customers to better understand
their monthly charges.

Section 3 is the effective date.

 
DIFFERENCE BETWEEN ORIGINAL AND AMENDED VERSIONS (IF APPLICABLE):

The A-print only includes original bill sections 2 and 3, and technical
changes were made to the original effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This legislation aims to provide greater transparency in the billing of
residential and commercial electric customers. This level of transparen-
cy will allow residential and commercial customers to better understand
their bills for energy consumption and will enable them to more accu-
rately project costs over time.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019-2020: S.7708 - Passed the Senate

 
STATE AND LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the one hundred eightieth day after it
shall have become a law.

summary: Updates certain requirements regarding billing for electric services, such as when corporations shall use an approved demand measuring device, mandating that classifications of service, the account and/or meter number, and the quantity billed be indicated on customers' bills.
